enriched_description: Dark grey American fox with a distinctive grizzled grey coat. Coat is thick and dense with a soft undercoat and longer guard hairs, grizzled grey on the back and sides with a reddish-brown neck and sides of head, white underside, and black stripe along the tail. Body is small, slender, and well-proportioned with short legs and a narrow chest. Head is broad with a flat skull and pointed muzzle. Ears are medium-sized, pointed, and erect. Tail is long, bushy, and black-tipped with a distinctive black stripe along the top. Eyes are medium-sized, almond-shaped, and dark with an alert, intelligent expression. The breed's signature features include its grizzled grey coat and black-tipped tail with dorsal stripe.

Domestic cat with a distinctive grey or tawny coat mottled with black in a tabby pattern. Coat features characteristic M-shaped marking on the forehead, dark stripes along the body, and ringed tail. Pattern types include classic (swirled), mackerel (striped), spotted, or ticked. Body is medium-sized, well-proportioned, and muscular. Head is round with a short muzzle. Ears are medium-sized, pointed, and erect. Eyes are large, round, and green, gold, or copper. The breed's signature features include the distinctive tabby pattern with M forehead marking and striped legs.

Domestic cat with a distinctive striped coat resembling tiger markings. Coat features bold, dark stripes on a lighter background (orange, brown, or grey) running vertically along the body. Pattern is typically mackerel tabby with narrow, parallel stripes. Body is medium-sized, athletic, and well-proportioned. Head is round with a short muzzle. Ears are medium-sized, pointed, and erect. Eyes are large, round, and green, gold, or copper. The breed's signature features include its bold tiger-like stripes and athletic build.

Long-haired breed of cat with a distinctive luxurious, flowing coat in various solid colors, tabby, bicolor, or calico patterns. Coat is long, thick, and silky with a dense undercoat and abundant ruff around the neck. Body is cobby, compact, and well-muscled with short legs. Head is round and massive with a short, snub nose and broad cheeks. Ears are small, rounded, set wide apart, and tipped forward. Eyes are large, round, and brilliant copper, gold, green, or blue. The breed's signature features include its long, flowing coat, flat face, and round, expressive eyes.

Slender, short-haired cat with distinctive color-point pattern. Coat is short, fine, and glossy with a pale body (cream, fawn, or white) and darker points on ears, face, paws, and tail in seal, chocolate, blue, or lilac. Body is long, slender, and tubular with fine bone structure. Head is wedge-shaped with a straight profile and large, pointed ears. Eyes are medium-sized, almond-shaped, slanted toward the nose, and vivid blue. Tail is long, thin, and tapering. The breed's signature features include its color-point pattern, blue almond-shaped eyes, and slender, elegant build.

Domestic cat of Egypt, typically referring to the Egyptian Mau or similar breeds. Coat is short to medium-length with distinctive spotted tabby pattern in silver, bronze, or smoke. Body is medium-sized, muscular, and well-proportioned with a distinctive flap of skin extending from the flank to the hind knee. Head is slightly rounded with a moderate muzzle. Ears are medium to large, alert, and set wide apart. Eyes are large, gooseberry-green, and almond-shaped. The breed's signature features include its naturally spotted coat, green eyes, and distinctive skin flap.

Large American feline resembling a lion with a uniform tawny coat. Coat is short, dense, and uniform in color ranging from greyish-brown to reddish-brown with a lighter underside. Body is large, muscular, and well-proportioned with long, powerful legs and a long tail. Head is small relative to body size with a broad skull and short muzzle. Ears are small, rounded, and erect with black backs. Tail is long, thick, and black-tipped. Eyes are medium-sized, round, and green, gold, or amber with an intense, alert expression. The breed's signature features include its uniform tawny coat, long tail, and powerful, athletic build.

Short-tailed wildcat with distinctive tufted ears and usually spotted or streaked coat. Coat is thick and dense with a soft undercoat, ranging from greyish-brown to reddish-brown with dark spots or streaks. Body is medium-sized, muscular, and well-proportioned with long legs and large, broad paws. Head is broad with a short muzzle. Ears are large, pointed, and erect with distinctive black tufts at the tips. Tail is very short and black-tipped. Eyes are medium-sized, round, and yellow-green with an alert expression. The breed's signature features include its ear tufts, short tail, and large snowshoe-like paws.

Large feline of African and Asian forests with a distinctive tawny coat covered in black rosettes. Coat is short, dense, and golden-tawny with black spots arranged in rosette patterns (clusters of spots forming ring-like shapes). Body is large, muscular, and well-proportioned with powerful legs and a long tail. Head is broad with a short muzzle. Ears are small, rounded, and erect with white spots on the back. Tail is long, thick, and ringed with black. Eyes are medium-sized, round, and golden-yellow with an intense, alert expression. The breed's signature features include its rosette-patterned coat and powerful, stealthy build.

Large feline of upland central Asia with distinctive long, thick whitish fur. Coat is thick, dense, and smoky-grey to yellowish-white with dark grey to black rosettes and spots. Fur is exceptionally long and dense, especially on the belly and tail, providing insulation in cold mountain environments. Body is large, muscular, and well-proportioned with short legs and broad paws. Head is small with a short muzzle. Ears are small, rounded, and erect. Tail is exceptionally long and thick, used for balance and warmth. Eyes are medium-sized, round, and pale green or grey with an intense expression. The breed's signature features include its thick whitish coat, long tail, and high-altitude habitat.
